text.display: When a car turns a corner, its outer wheel has to travel farther than the inner wheel. So the two wheels must spin at different speeds, and the differential makes that possible. The engine turns a ring gear and its carrier, and small planet gears inside link the two axles. On a curve, the planet gears start to turn, so one wheel speeds up while the other slows down. And the carrier always moves at the average speed of the two wheels.
